# Synapse 2.0.6

A security release: it updates the libraries Synapse is built on. Upgrade now, especially if you run Synapse on Windows or let other devices on your network open it.

## Security

- **The app's web server (Next.js 16.4.5).** Fixes a remote code execution that needs no sign-in on Windows, and several in image optimization, along with request-forgery and denial-of-service issues. Synapse's web app runs on every install, so every install should take this.
- **Images (Pillow 13).** Fixes memory and crash bugs in reading PNG, JPEG, TIFF and other images. Knowledge reads every image you upload, so a crafted file could reach them.
- **Trusted certificates (certifi).** Removes certificate authorities whose keys were compromised, for every secure connection Synapse makes.
- **Other libraries:** aiohttp (the browser's helper server), urllib3, PyJWT, oauthlib, pypdf, pyasn1, filelock, setuptools and Docling, each to a fixed release. The image library behind the web server (sharp) and its build tools move with Next.js.

## Fixed

- **Schedules save in your own timezone in Docker.** The Docker images had no timezone database, so a schedule in any place's local time was refused ("'Asia/Calcutta' is not a place's timezone"), and only UTC worked. Synapse now brings its own copy of the timezone database, so every install reads every zone, including older names a browser may send, such as Asia/Calcutta.

## Changed

- **Connecting to MCP servers is stricter.** When connecting to an MCP server, Synapse no longer follows a redirect to a different site, and refuses a sign-in server that doesn't match the one the server named. A server that relied on either now fails to connect with an error, instead of quietly connecting somewhere else.
- **Documents read with Docling are read again once.** Docling is newer, so a document it read before is read again the next time Knowledge opens it.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.6`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
